bifrost: springboard/render/src/gfx.rs (CPU blur), springboard/src/gpu/wl.rs (GPU dual-Kawase blur pyramid), springboard/render/src/gfx/rotate.rs (bilinear resample), springboard/render/src/emoji.rs (area and bilinear resample), springboard/src/gpu/egl.rs (EGL/GLES compute and render path)
summary: BifrOSt has a GPU blur pyramid and bilinear resampling, both used internally by the shell for glass and scaling. It exposes no app-facing GPU image-filter, histogram, matrix or neural-network API, and only a unary kernel base trait with a chain runner (springboard/render/src/kernel.rs), not a Metal-style kernel layer; most of the framework has no counterpart.

features.bifrost: springboard/src/gpu/egl.rs (EGL/GLES device init on Mesa via GBM)
features.note: Metal-only device query. BifrOSt uses EGL/GLES on Linux, so the Apple call has no direct counterpart.

features.feature: Neural network graphs and CNN layers
features.apple: MPSNNGraph, MPSCNNConvolutionNode, MPSCNNPoolingNode, MPSCNNFullyConnectedNode and the other layer nodes
features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/cnn_layers.rs (Network, Layer, conv2d, pool2d, dense, relu); tests: springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-complete-22.rs
features.note: A Network chains convolution, pooling, dense, relu and custom layers, checks every shape before it runs, and is tested headless. Gap: there is no graph object, no node classes for apps, no GPU path and no serialised model.

LSTM and GRU single steps are implemented, and the tests check a bounded LSTM state over a sequence and the refusal of a hidden state of the wrong length. Gap: there is no sequence layer that runs many steps, no training layer and no matrix inference layer for apps.

features.feature: Matrix and vector kernels (multiply, decomposition, solve, softmax)
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 15 tests. Wave 4 (w4-metal-performance-shaders, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No GPU linear algebra in springboard.
Ray intersection is not a desktop-shell need, and the framework's acceleration structure classes are deprecated in the Apple docs.

features.feature: Kernel base classes and keyed archiving
features.apple: MPSKernel, MPSUnaryImageKernel, MPSBinaryImageKernel, NSKeyedArchiver with MPSKeyedUnarchiver
features.note: An app defines a kernel by implementing ImageKernel with its class, the built-in kernels implement it too, and apply_chain runs kernels in order; all tested headless. Gap: there is no GPU kernel dispatch, no keyed archiving of kernels, and the code is not wired into the shell or apps.

gaps: No app-facing GPU compute or image-filter API. The GPU path (springboard/src/gpu/) serves the shell only.

No app-facing convolution with a caller kernel and no app-facing image statistics; plane_stats is shell-side. Histogram, threshold, morphology, median, Sobel and Laplacian are app-facing in sdk pixel_filter (2026-10-17).

No graph object and no GPU path for neural network layers. CPU layers exist (ui cnn_layers: convolution, pooling, dense, relu, LSTM and GRU steps; sdk core_ml: dense, relu and softmax models), but apps cannot build a graph or serialise a model beyond its text form.
No GPU matrix or linear algebra kernels. CPU vector, matrix and quaternion types are in sdk linear_algebra.
Resampling is bilinear or area-average in the shell. Lanczos is the LanczosScale kernel in ui image_kernels, with no sdk resample call.
